attribution.note: Zitron's own words on his own newsletter, stated firmly and endorsed.

semantics.note: Narrowing the scope to OpenAI/Anthropic subscriptions matches the context. 'No way to fix' looks forward but is phrased as a present-tense assertion. Treating it as an observation is acceptable.

contract.note: The speaker named no metric or period, so the Q1 2026 period, subscription-level costing and the 'no feasible remedy' bar are all evaluator inferences. The plain reading is ordinary. The unbounded 'no way to fix' clause makes support hard to reach either way.

evidence.note: Anthropic S-1 filed before the evaluation date. It covers company-wide net losses, which are dominated by fair-value changes. It says nothing on subscription-level economics or remedies.
June 2026 secondary report valuing maximum usage at retail API prices. That is not provider serving cost, and it falls outside the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: The claim needs subscription-level revenue against attributable serving cost, plus evidence that no remedy exists. The packet has only Anthropic's company-wide losses and a retail-API-value estimate, and neither measures subscription economics for either provider. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own conditional assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Both company branches keep their antecedents: for OpenAI, revenue shortfall plus no funding or debt; for Anthropic, capacity built plus no tens of billions a month. 'Will' makes it a firm conditional forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: Treating the companies as separate branches, defining running out of money as a liquidity failure, and requiring the antecedents to be verified first are all faithful to the wording.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure of $122B in committed capital on 2026-03-31. It goes to the financing antecedent but does not settle a future revenue shortfall or liquidity.
Anthropic's May 2026 Series H disclosure. These are financing commitments, not realized revenue or cash. The antecedent is not established.
April 2026 announcement of staged future capacity. It does not show that the contemplated buildout is complete.

reviews.rationale: Neither company's antecedent is established. The evidence shows OpenAI obtained large financing, and Anthropic's capacity is only partly scheduled. Neither company has run out of money. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent is unknown is not scored, and with no deadline the forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own generalization in his post.

semantics.note: The universal 'every' is kept, along with the three named categories. It is a hyperbolic but firm descriptive claim about published agent stories.

contract.note: The contract separates executing transactions from content generation, which is an ordinary reading. The speaker reduces actions like reminders or spam removal to his categories, but stretching 'generating something' to cover every action would make the claim unfalsifiable. The result turns on this reading.

evidence.note: A dated December 2025 published story, before the post, describing an AI agent that sources items, sets prices and executes sales. That is running a shop, outside the three categories.
Phase one of the same project (June 2025) shows the agent performed poorly. The claim concerns what stories are about, not success, so this does not undercut the counterexample.

reviews.rationale: A universal claim falls to a single counterexample. Project Vend's published accounts, available before 2026-04-14, describe an AI agent running a shop and executing sales, which is not code generation, summarization or content generation on an ordinary reading. The interpretive dependence is noted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Will' plus 'mere months' makes this a firm forecast. The sentence says 'different', but the context (degrade, twist the knife) points to deterioration in both quality and availability.

contract.note: The contextual deterioration reading and the six-month window are ordinary interpretations, though the speaker supplied neither. A direction-neutral reading would weigh the evidence differently.

evidence.note: Anthropic disclosed a coding-quality regression from April 16 that was reverted April 20. It was transient and does not establish a material change in quality over months.
From May 2026, Anthropic doubled Claude Code rate limits on its paid plans. That is a material access improvement, against the predicted deterioration for that provider.
OpenAI's October 2026 GPT-6 rollout shows a changed product but does not measure quality or access deterioration.

reviews.rationale: On the deterioration reading, Anthropic's access improved and its brief quality regression was reverted, which cuts against the forecast. There is no comparable quality or access evidence for OpenAI, and nothing establishes broadly maintained quality. The packet therefore neither shows deterioration in both dimensions nor meets the contract's broad contradiction condition.
